questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The classes I could take were the most important, as well as the language the classes were in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, the Erasmus office was always replying very fast.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got help from a friend who had studied there the semester before, and then I met some Erasmus organisations, and also got a lot of help from the Erasmus office at the host university itself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the website HousingAnywhere, which is a website I got recommended when I was on exchange last year in Madrid. It has worked fine both times.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are lots of possibilities in Salamanca and since it's a university city it is easy to find housing in areas with other students. Most of the time housing off campus is also cheaper than on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to go physically to their erasmus office, and fill out some paperwork, but it was very simple and I only had to go one time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The erasmus office at the university

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted and didn't have to change during the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To ask all the questions you may have, the erasmus office are very sweet and take their time to help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose courses that were in the last year of their bachelor (4th year of university), because of this the courses requiered that you had studied beforehand, and I noticed this level both in the teachers as well as the students who shared a knowledge and compassion of the topics studied. The level fitted quite perfectly for me.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They give you much more homework and assignments that you have to do, and in most of my classes you also had to participate actively in class to be able to get a good grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Ética y Teoría Feminista
Pensamiento Filosófico II
Estética de las Creaciones Literarias
Historia de la Filosofía Española e Iberoamericana
Literaturas Europeas Contemporáneas

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Literaturas Europeas Contemporáneas was an especially international class, because we were mostly exchange students. However, one of my favorite courses was Ética and Teoría Feminista, where we were only two exchange students, however, the teacher was very nice to include us and it was especially an interesting class because I got to compare feminism in spain and latinamerica vs. my own country.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs, however I did choose to go travelling, which also adds to the budget.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I found out that my housing was quite expensive compared to what the spanish students were paying

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We were never introduced to the different activities available, so you had to go out and find it yourself I took a painting course directed by one of the student organisations.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The painting course was a really fun way to meet other exchange students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of places close by where you can go hiking. Apart from that, the train to Madrid is really cheap, so it's easy to go on a daytrip to Madrid or continue from there to other places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me, since I've been living in Spain before. The students were very open to include me in their activities.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and ask quesitons. Most students at the university of Salamanca actually come from different parts in Spain, this means they are usually more open to talk to exchange students as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Getting used to the spanish timetable, especially since Salamanca is a smaller city all the shops and restaurants close in the middle of the day during siesta.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of festivities where all of the city joined in. Especially the classical guitar music is something I enjoyed very much.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. To prioritize studying during the semester, otherwise you won't have enough time to study for the exams.
2. Take time to search for activities, they might be hard to see at first but there's actually a lot of student sports etc. 
3. Make some spanish friends, you'll get better at the language and they might help you if you need notes or other help for the studies.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: In general they requiere a lot to get a good grade, so it's a good tactic to study persistently all through the semester so you don't drown in studies at the end. That said, don't forget to enjoy the Erasmus life!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have definitely learned a lot in my classes and I have become much more independent in my studies. This is a maturity I will bring with me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For personal reasons I felt a bit lonely in the beginning of my stay, however, I was lucky to find some very good friends later on. I would say it's good to try and make as many friends as possible especially in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
